scores.evidence: Delivery is at-least-once. Consumers deduplicate on `decision_id` or `auth_id`.
scores.rationale: Mostly correct on Redis Lua hash-tag atomicity, CEL, ONNX, and at-least-once; minor issues (merchant key in a separate slot, Lua atomic dedupe described loosely, in-flight duplicate handling, BIN 8 digits, counter loss after failover) have small design consequence.

scores.evidence: a fraud-decision service that the issuer's existing Auth Host ... calls during each authorisation. It returns APPROVE, DECLINE, APPROVE_AND_ALERT or NO_DECISION
scores.rationale: Solves the real inline problem with explicit assumptions, essential vs optional separated, and explicit non-goals (3DS, case mgmt, graph) with reasons; step-up is excluded, a small gap.

scores.evidence: Only `decision-service` is on the authorisation path. Its single synchronous dependency is Redis.
scores.rationale: Clear ownership of Redis keys and data flows; small loose ends such as merchant key slotting and the 'single dependency' claim versus the snapshot bucket.

scores.evidence: Out-of-time test set with labels ≥ 90 days old ... PSI < 0.2 on shadow traffic ... Gatling at peak and 1.7× peak
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, spikes come early, targets are labeled as assumptions, shadow and holdout cohorts continue after launch.

scores.evidence: all targets are assumptions until confirmed in Spikes S2 and S3
scores.rationale: Assumption table gives impact if wrong and how/when each is validated, plus open questions with defaults.

scores.evidence: Redis misses its deadline or is unavailable: evaluate only the request-only rules (block lists). If one fires, return DECLINE; otherwise NO_DECISION
scores.rationale: Covers Redis failover, duplicates, Kafka outage, bad rules, poisoned labels, insider allow-list and feedback bias; some gaps like out-of-order and reversal handling and model-drift response.

scores.evidence: Rollback, at three levels, each tested in M2: ... kill switch ... Runbooks (M2)
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, monitoring, ownership, runbooks and on-call are concrete and sized to the team; schema migration and access admin less detailed.

scores.evidence: Prod is about $3–6k/month: Fargate: 6–10 tasks. Redis ... MSK
scores.rationale: Drivers listed with controls, but estimate is unbacked, scaling with usage is thin, and the storage claim of 15 GB/day with 7-year retention and 'storage cost unlikely significant' is questionable; no build cost.

scores.evidence: Hard to add later, because history can't be logged after the fact
scores.rationale: Reversibility column for each decision, hard ones (Auth Host contract, feature logging, PAN scope, language) identified and spikes early, exit paths named.

scores.evidence: One `decision-service` deployable plus a small `outcome-worker` ... There is no rules UI in v1.
scores.rationale: Simplest workable design, no stream cluster, rules in Git, deferrals with triggers; MSK and separate ML account a bit heavy but justified.

scores.evidence: T1 first, on day 1. ... Done when: Testcontainers tests cover window edges, duplicates, in-flight duplicates, and 100 concurrent requests
scores.rationale: Task-level breakdown with locations, done-criteria, dependency ordering, and spike outcomes that change the plan.

checklist.evidence: Server-side p99 ≤ 50 ms ... Expected p99 is about 20 ms; each module with a deadline (Redis 20 ms, rules ≤3 ms, model ≤2 ms)
On a timeout or NO_DECISION it applies its existing static rules ... Fail-open policy: ... Default: Apply existing static rules
Card features are computed during the request with one atomic Redis script ... The exact feature values used for each decision are logged and reused for training
Monthly training uses decisions older than 90 days, whose labels are mostly in ... Out-of-time test set with labels ≥ 90 days old
Catch ≥ 60% of fraud value at false-positive ratio ≤ 8:1. Alerts ≤ 1,500/day
Policy ... block-list → allow-list → hard rules → model threshold → alert rules; actions APPROVE, DECLINE, APPROVE_AND_ALERT (no step-up)
Building a case-management tool. We integrate with the existing one ... customer "yes, that was me" replies flow through label-ingest-job
Never received: PAN, CVV2, PIN block, track data, expiry date. The contract rejects any of these fields, and a test checks it.
Topics are keyed by card_token, with 24 partitions ... Consumers deduplicate on decision_id or auth_id
Shadow scoring on live traffic before enforcement ... champion/challenger shadow scoring ... Score distribution ... bad model (revert the manifest PR)
100% of decisions can be reconstructed (inputs, features, rule-set version, model version, output) for 7 years
at least 6 Fargate tasks ... spread across 3 AZs, so losing one AZ still leaves enough capacity for peak ... 3,000 TPS design peak

traps.evidence: Inline synchronous decision, with Auth Host fallback on timeout or NO_DECISION
The Auth Host waits at most 150 ms. On a timeout or NO_DECISION it applies its existing static rules
Out-of-time test set with labels ≥ 90 days old
The exact bucketing is written down in contracts/features/feature-set-v1.yaml, and the offline code has to copy it exactly.
No card numbers (PANs) or other sensitive card data enter the system. It only sees a card token and the BIN

note: Very strong, well-grounded inline fraud plan with explicit assumptions and early spikes; weaker on step-up actions, out-of-order/reversal handling, and cost grounding.
